title: Cornyn’s Defeat Fuels Tensions With President Trump in Senate G.O.P.
partialText: Senators are angry President Trump turned on a respected former leader whom they consider a loyal Republican. Now Mr. Trump faces resistance from his own embittered ranks.

title: Paxton’s Texas Victory Opens a New Front in the Battle for the Senate
partialText: Many Democrats and some Republicans said the scandal-plagued Ken Paxton’s victory could turn Texas into a battleground state that will determine Senate control.

title: A Blue Texas May Be More Than a Dream for Democrats
partialText: Ken Paxton’s victory for the Republican nomination and a big shift among Hispanic voters have put a Senate seat within reach.

title: Alabama Republicans Ask Supreme Court to Allow New Congressional Map in Redistricting Fight
partialText: Republican leaders in the state have asked the justices to clear the way for a congressional map that a lower court found discriminated against Black voters.

title: Reflecting Pool Contract Has ‘Inflated’ Profit Margin, Government Analysis Finds
partialText: The firm that was given a no-bid contract to fix the troubled landmark is charging 20 percent. The typical profit margin is 6 percent to 12 percent, internal records show.

title: National Park Entrance Fees Are Funding Trump’s D.C. Projects
partialText: The administration is spending at least $67 million worth of fees paid by visitors to national parks on fixing D.C. fountains and the Reflecting Pool.

title: Israel Continues Its Escalation in Lebanon, Ordering Evacuations
partialText: The Israeli military issued sweeping evacuation orders for two southern cities, indicating that more airstrikes were imminent.

title: Residents Watch as Israeli War Planes Circle Over Southern Lebanon
partialText: Israel has intensified its deadly military campaign against Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militant group, in recent days, striking targets across Lebanon.

title: Global Supply Shortages Deepen as War Drags On, Risking Jobs and Growth
partialText: After three months, the fallout of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is spreading, with developing countries bearing the brunt of the shortfall.

title: A Quiet Pacific Village Becomes China’s Security Testing Ground
partialText: When a remote Pacific village asked for help with rowdy youth, the Chinese police arrived with a surveillance system. Then came the backlash.

title: Biden Sues Justice Dept. to Block Release of Tapes
partialText: The former president argued that the Justice Department has a responsibility to protect the privacy of conversations he had with a former ghostwriter.

title: ’60 Minutes’ Journalist Sharyn Alfonsi Loses Deal After Dispute With Bari Weiss
partialText: Sharyn Alfonsi, whose segment on a brutal Salvadoran prison was pulled abruptly in December, said that CBS News and its top editor, Bari Weiss, had let her contract expire.

title: The $400 Million Showdown Between a Billionaire and a California Mayor
partialText: The owner of the Los Angeles Rams and the City of Inglewood are in a dispute over Hollywood Park and SoFi Stadium, which is about to host World Cup matches.

title: Rubio’s India Visit Yields No Major Deals to Repair U.S.-India Relations
partialText: The secretary of state visited India to reassure the South Asian giant that it can still rely on the United States. India did not gain much from the visit.

title: Thornton Wilder’s Last Play Vanished Into Thin Air. Or Did It?
partialText: Decades after “The Emporium” failed to open on Broadway in 1954, one man went on a quest to find it.

title: The Viruses Causing New Outbreaks Are Much Less Familiar to Science
partialText: The types of Ebola and hantavirus worrying officials are very different from the species identified decades ago, raising new questions about how to respond.

title: Uganda Closes Border With Congo Over Ebola Fears
partialText: Ebola response teams and a few others are exempt and will undergo “strict health screening,” a top Ugandan official said.

title: Ferrari’s First Electric Car Runs Into Backlash in Italy and Beyond
partialText: Memes mocked the new model, analysts questioned its appeal and investors sold the automaker’s stock. A former Ferrari chairman warned of “the destruction of a legend.”

title: Could Russia Hit Harder? It at Least Wants Ukraine to Think So.
partialText: Major attacks on Kyiv, followed by warnings of more, come as Moscow is stalled on the battlefield and at the negotiating table.

title: High-Level British Spy Warns of Expanding Russia Threat
partialText: The director of Britain’s electronic surveillance agency warned that Moscow was getting more brazen, adding that estimates suggested 500,000 Russian soldiers had been killed in the Ukraine war.

title: Knicks Fans Confront High Ticket Prices for NBA Finals Games at MSG
partialText: New York Knicks fans, still celebrating the team making it to the N.B.A. finals, are confronting high ticket prices for the games at Madison Square Garden.

title: Tiler Peck’s New Ballet Expands the Idea of What Female and Male Dancers Can Be
partialText: The idea of sisterhood and brotherhood flows through “Symphonie Espagnole,” Peck’s new work for New York City Ballet. We dissect two sections.

title: Writing Is Fundamental to How We Think
partialText: A.I. can be a crutch that hurts our ability to think creatively.

title: Time Gave Me Back What Prison Took Away
partialText: A formerly incarcerated writer reflects on how the prison system didn’t foster change, but befriending time did.

title: War. Heat. Cigarettes.
partialText: Updates on stories from around the world.

title: Ball State Settles With Ex-Employee for $225,000 Over Charlie Kirk Posts
partialText: Ball State University is the latest institution to agree to pay workers who lost their jobs over their posts about the conservative activist.

title: After Decades on the Run, a Leftist Militant Is Sentenced in Germany
partialText: Daniela Klette, 67, was part of the Red Army Faction, which attacked American and capitalist interests until the 1990s. She was convicted of robberies committed later to finance life as a fugitive.

title: Where Time Is Always 15 Minutes Apart From Everywhere Else
partialText: In Nepal, a nation wedged between India and China, a unique time zone is just one expression of a singular national identity.

title: Teachers Union Urges Schools to Curb A.I. Chatbots and Screen Time
partialText: The American Federation of Teachers recommended “no screens” at all for those in second grade or younger, and no A.I. chatbots for students in elementary school.
